confidentiality.ex: An HR file is encrypted so only authorized managers can read it.

integrity.ex: A system checks a downloaded file's hash to confirm it was not altered.

availability.ex: Redundant servers are deployed so the service stays reachable if one fails.

non repudiation.ex: A contract is digitally signed, so the sender cannot later deny sending it.

least privilege.ex: An intern is given read-only access to just the folder they need, nothing more.

defense in depth.ex: Firewall, antivirus and strong authentication stack up so one flaw is not enough.

separation of duties.ex: The person who enters an invoice cannot also approve it, to prevent fraud.

need to know.ex: A Secret-cleared officer only accesses the files strictly required for their mission.

accountability.ex: Every sensitive action is logged and tied to the user who performed it.

due care.ex: The company deploys reasonable protections, as a prudent actor would.

due diligence.ex: The team regularly verifies that security measures remain effective over time.

multi factor authentication.ex: To log in, the user enters a password and then a code sent to their phone.

role based access control.ex: Rights are assigned by job function: every accountant has the same access.

discretionary access control.ex: The owner of a file decides who may access it.

mandatory access control.ex: The system enforces access from classification labels; users cannot override it.

single sign on.ex: One login grants access to email, intranet and HR applications.

privilege escalation.ex: An attacker exploits a flaw to move from a user account to an administrator account.

privileged access management.ex: Administrator accounts are vaulted and their sessions recorded.

biometrics.ex: Access to the server room is granted by fingerprint.

provisioning.ex: When an employee joins, their accounts and access are created automatically for their role.

deprovisioning.ex: When an employee leaves, all their access is revoked immediately.

risk acceptance.ex: Management chooses to live with a low risk rather than invest to reduce it.

risk avoidance.ex: A risky feature is dropped to eliminate the risk entirely.

risk mitigation.ex: A firewall is installed to lower the likelihood of an intrusion.

risk transference.ex: The company buys cyber-insurance to transfer part of the risk.

residual risk.ex: After all controls are applied, a remaining level of risk is documented.

annualized loss expectancy.ex: Expected yearly loss is estimated by multiplying loss per incident by its annual frequency.

business impact analysis.ex: Critical functions and the impact of their outage are identified before building the continuity plan.

symmetric encryption.ex: Two parties share one secret key to encrypt and decrypt their exchanges.

asymmetric encryption.ex: A message is encrypted with the recipient's public key; only their private key decrypts it.

hashing.ex: A password's irreversible fingerprint is stored instead of the password itself.

digital signature.ex: A document is cryptographically signed, proving its author and integrity.

public key infrastructure.ex: A certificate authority issues and manages the organization's digital certificates.

salt.ex: A random value is added to each password before hashing to defeat precomputed tables.

tls.ex: The browser padlock shows the connection to the site is encrypted in transit.

firewall.ex: A device filters traffic between the internal network and the Internet using rules.

intrusion detection system.ex: A sensor analyses traffic and alerts the team on suspicious activity, without blocking it.

intrusion prevention system.ex: A device detects a network attack and blocks it automatically.

vpn.ex: A remote worker sets up an encrypted tunnel to reach the corporate network.

demilitarized zone.ex: The public web server is placed in a buffer subnet, isolated from the internal network.

network segmentation.ex: The industrial network is separated from the office network to limit an attack's spread.

zero trust.ex: No connection is implicitly trusted: every access is verified, even internally.

network access control.ex: A device must prove its compliance before being admitted to the network.

phishing.ex: A fraudulent email imitates the bank to trick the victim into entering their credentials.

spear phishing.ex: A highly personalized email targets the chief financial officer specifically.

sql injection.ex: An attacker inserts SQL into a form field to read the database.

cross site scripting.ex: A malicious script is injected into a page and runs in other visitors' browsers.

ransomware.ex: Software encrypts the company's files and demands a ransom to release them.

social engineering.ex: A stranger poses as IT support to obtain a password.

piggybacking tailgating.ex: An unauthorized person enters the premises by following an employee who badged in.

evil twin.ex: A rogue Wi-Fi access point imitates the hotel's to intercept guests' traffic.

pass the hash.ex: The attacker authenticates with a stolen password hash, without knowing the password.

man in the middle.ex: An attacker sits between two parties to eavesdrop on their communication.

distributed denial of service.ex: Thousands of machines flood a site with requests to make it unavailable.

rainbow table.ex: The attacker uses a table of precomputed hashes to recover passwords quickly.

honeypot.ex: A decoy server is deployed to lure attackers and study their methods.

containment.ex: On detection, the infected machine is isolated from the network to stop the spread.

eradication.ex: The malware is removed and the exploited flaw is fixed.

chain of custody.ex: Every handling of an evidence item is logged so it stays admissible in court.

recovery time objective.ex: A 4-hour maximum is set to restore the service after an outage.

recovery point objective.ex: At most 15 minutes of data loss is accepted, which sets the backup frequency.

hot site.ex: A fully equipped alternate site lets operations resume within minutes.

shared responsibility model.ex: The provider secures the infrastructure; the customer secures their data and access.

software as a service.ex: The company uses a ready-to-use online mail service with nothing to install.

infrastructure as a service.ex: The team rents virtual servers and manages the operating system itself.

cloud access security broker.ex: An intermediary enforces security policy between users and cloud services.

data sovereignty.ex: Data hosted in a country is subject to that country's laws.

tokenization.ex: A card number is replaced by a token with no exploitable value if stolen.

data loss prevention.ex: A tool blocks emailing a file that contains social security numbers.

droit à l effacement.ex: Un client demande la suppression de toutes ses données : l'entreprise doit y donner suite.

notifier l autorité sous 72 h.ex: Après une fuite de données, l'entreprise dispose de 72 heures pour prévenir la CNIL.

analyse d impact aipd.ex: Avant un traitement à risque élevé, on évalue formellement son impact sur la vie privée.

consentement.ex: Une case non pré-cochée invite l'utilisateur à accepter explicitement le traitement de ses données.

habilitation.ex: Une décision formelle autorise un agent à accéder aux informations classifiées d'un niveau donné.

homologation d un si classifié.ex: Une autorité atteste qu'un système atteint le niveau de sécurité requis avant sa mise en service.
